newsitem.title: USA: Sportmart to boost ad spending after Canadian exit.
newsitem.headline: Sportmart to boost ad spending after Canadian exit.

text.p: Sportmart Inc, which Thursday announced plans to exit the Canadian market, plans to use the $3.5 million to $4.5 million it expects to save annually on increased advertising and to continue a previously annunced remodeling program, a company official said.

"We're looking to increasing our ad budget for 1997," Tom Hendrickson, Sportmart's chief financial officer, told Reuters. "We'll also decide which (U.S.) markets we want to focus on for our remodeling progrsm."

Sportmart said earlier it will close its 11 stores in four Canadian markets and take a charge of between $18 million and $21 million, after related income tax benefits, in the fourth quarter. The retailer also said all of its Canadian inventory should be liquidated by the end of its fiscal first quarter.
About 600 Sportmart employees in Canada will be affected by the store closings, Hendrickson said.
Hendrickson and other Sportmart officials blamed increased competition in Canada since Sportmart opened its first stores in Toronto in 1995 for a sharp decline in recent sales.
"Sports Authority has five stores in Toronto and Forzani is also a presence where we were operating," he said.
Sports Authority is a division of Kmart Corp. The Forzani chain is owned by Forzani Group Ltd of Canada.
Sportmart is scheduled to hold a conference call with investors Friday morning to discuss the Canadian shutdown and other future plans.
